rationale: Three lenses ran (blind, edge-case, acceptance) over a 160-line diff; the core fix is correct and matches both the ticket and the repo's own icon-button guide — role, accessible name and aria-hidden on both decorative icons are verified by passing tests against real SVGR output. Four major findings survive triage, all introduced or left open by this change: no visible focus indicator on a control this diff makes Tab-reachable for the first time (repo guide marks it mandatory), focus dropped to <body> after a row is removed, duplicate accessible names when two rows share a file name, and the ticket's 'for all delete file buttons' clause left unmet for the two other file-delete controls whose icons still lack aria-hidden. Four blind-lens suspicions were investigated and refuted against source (nested interactive dropzone root, Enter-key bubbling opening the file picker, tailwind class-merge losing the hover colour, per-list index mapping) — DropzoneArea is a plain div with no role/tabIndex/onKeyDown, keyboard activation synthesises a click that the existing stopPropagation catches, cn() uses twMerge, and FileList indexes each list separately. 2 findings dismissed; 1 deferred (row height grows ~4px because Button SMALL is h-6 against the previous bare size-4 icon — cosmetic, verify on the MR screenshots).

aria-label={`Delete file ${fileName}`} spread onto the DOM button; asserted via getByRole name query.

business_review.criterion: The X image is hidden from assistive technologies
business_review.evidence: XMarkSvg aria-hidden="true"; asserted against real SVGR output with no icon mocking.
Native button; test tabs to it, asserts focus, presses Enter, onRemove called once.

Role+name satisfied on every file-delete control in the app, but the icons in SkillBundleFilesSection and File.tsx still lack aria-hidden. See CR-002.

Implementation and both test files match plan Tasks 1-2; lint clean, typecheck clean, unit 4177 passed, integration 468 passed 1 skipped.

standards_review.notes: Both commits use the documented 'EPMCDME-8559: <subject>' form on branch EPMCDME-8559_accessible-delete-file-button cut from main.
aria-label on the button, aria-hidden on the decorative icons — exactly the guide's example.
Raised as CR-001; blocking because the guide lists it as a Pre-Delivery Checklist item and this diff is what puts the control in the tab order.
Apache-2.0 headers present on new files; no lint or typecheck violations; no new dependency.
No auth, secrets, network, or file-content handling in the diff.

findings.problem: The delete control is Tab-reachable for the first time but has no designed focus indicator. Neither the call site nor Button.tsx defines any focus:/focus-visible: class, and the tertiary variant is bg-none border-none with only a hover state.
findings.impact: Shifts the defect from screen-reader users to sighted keyboard users (WCAG 2.4.7). The repo guide lists a visible focus ring as mandatory, and the repo already has ~27 focus-visible:ring-* usages showing the house style.
findings.recommendation: Add the established focus treatment to the button (focus:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-border-accent focus-visible:ring-offset-1), mirroring PinnedRow.tsx:44, and assert it in the unit test.

findings.problem: The ticket's 'for all delete file buttons' clause requires both an accessible name/role and the icon hidden from assistive technologies. The other two file-delete controls already have name and role, but their decorative icons (CrossSvg, FileSvg, BasketSvg, DownloadSvg) carry no aria-hidden.
findings.impact: Partial ticket coverage — those screens can still expose the icon as a graphics node and fail re-test under the same clause the QA engineer will read.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-hidden="true" to those decorative icons (one attribute each, zero behavioural risk), or state explicitly in the MR description and the ticket that they are deferred to a follow-up.

findings.problem: Nothing manages focus after activation: onRemove unmounts the row owning the focused button, so document.activeElement falls back to <body>. Verified — no ref and no focus() call anywhere in FileListItem, FileList or FilesDropzone.
findings.impact: Newly introduced by this diff (the control was previously unreachable). Deleting N files costs N full tab traversals from the document start (WCAG 2.4.3). Note the removal announcement itself is already covered by sibling ticket EPMCDME-8560's live region — do not duplicate it here.
findings.recommendation: After removal move focus to the next remaining row's delete button, falling back to the previous row and then to the drop area when the list empties. Compute the target in FileList, which owns the list. Cover it with a test.

findings.problem: The accessible name derives solely from fileName, which is not unique: FileDropArea.addFiles appends with no de-duplication and clears the input value after each pick, and uploadedFiles (already indexed server-side) and files (pending local) render into one list and can share a name. Two or more buttons then have byte-identical accessible names.
findings.impact: A screen-reader or voice-control user gets indistinguishable 'Delete file spec.pdf' buttons whose consequences differ materially — one drops an already-indexed server file via onUploadedFileRemove, the other only a pending local File. It also makes getByRole name queries throw on ambiguity, so future tests and Playwright locators break on duplicate-name lists.
findings.recommendation: Decision needed on naming: minimally distinguish the two sections ('Delete uploaded file X' vs 'Delete selected file X'), or fully disambiguate with row position, or mark it a follow-up because it is a pre-existing ambiguity this ticket only surfaces (before the change these controls had no accessible name at all, so it is not a regression).
